source: Pfungst (1911) Clever Hans (The Horse of Mr. von Osten), Project Gutenberg text
finding: Original text confirms the blinder test numbers. Large blinders (15 x 15 cm) were needed; small ones did not work. The test sorted trials into 'not seen', 'seen' and 'undecided'.
numbers: 102 blinder tests. Not seen: 35 tests, 6% correct (only two). Seen: 56 tests, 89% correct (about 50). Undecided: 11 tests, 18% correct.
quote: the horse required certain visual stimuli or signs in order to make a correct response
limits: Secondary reports give 50/56 and 2/35 and leave out the 11 undecided trials. Counts are tests, not independent animals or sessions. One horse.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 closed for Pfungst: the 2/35 vs 50/56 figures are right. Note the third 'undecided' bin: a cue check needs a clear rule for ambiguous trials.

source: Farrar, Ostojic and Clayton (2021) hidden side of animal cognition research (survey), PMC page re-opened
finding: Re-read the PMC page. Sample size and bias figures match the earlier line a14. 'Over 70%' endorse the canon is confirmed in the abstract text; the exact 70.5% string was not found in the page text I extracted.
numbers: 1001 invited; 969 emails sent successfully; 210 completed (21.6%). Hope for a result: sometimes 39.7%, often 38.8%. 73.0% say some areas could face a replication crisis if replicated.
limits: Self-selected 21.6% response. The 70.5% figure rests on the earlier read; here only 'over 70%' was seen.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 closed for Farrar: numbers match. Canon endorsement is high but is a self-report from a self-selected sample.

source: Krupenye et al. (2016) Great apes anticipate that other individuals will act according to false beliefs (abstract via Europe PMC)
finding: Abstract only. Three ape species look in anticipation of an agent acting on the false-belief location. Full text is paywalled; per-condition counts were not available.
numbers: None in the abstract. The 22/30 figure used in this folder comes from Kano 2017 (b03, b04), not from this paper.
limits: Abstract only, so opened is false. Counts remain second-hand.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays open for Krupenye numbers. Do not quote 22/30 as verified from the original.

source: Hare, Call and Tomasello (2001) Do chimpanzees know what conspecifics know? (abstract via Europe PMC)
finding: Abstract only. Subordinates preferred food the dominant had not seen hidden (experiment 1) and tracked which dominant had witnessed (experiment 2). Experiment 3 gave no consistent choice, which the authors put down to a changed competition, not missing skill.
limits: Abstract only. Later low-level rival accounts of this design were not re-checked here.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays open for Hare numbers. The authors explained their own null by task change, the same demand argument as Hu and Frank.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet (ICLR 2024)
finding: A forced second look without outside feedback often lowers accuracy. Without oracle labels the model changes right answers to wrong ones more often than the reverse. With oracle labels it looks good, which is the flaw in earlier reports.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after one round, 41.8 after two. GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 75.1 -> 74.7. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0. GPT-4 CommonSenseQA 82.0 -> 79.5 -> 80.0. Oracle-label version of GPT-3.5 GSM8K: 75.9 -> 95.5. Calls rise 1 -> 3 -> 5. GPT-3.5 kept its GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time.
quote: LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning
limits: Self-correction prompt asks to review for problems, which presses the model to change. Not a rival-hypothesis prompt, so a close analogue only. Small samples (100 for HotpotQA). Table columns were read from pdftotext layout and may be slightly misaligned.
agent_relevance: Nearest tested cousin of gap 1 and gap 10. A forced 'find the problem' step can cause false changes (like over-doubting). A rival-plus-probe operator must have a keep-the-answer exit and be compared to plain CoT at equal calls.

source: Gu et al. (2026) SimpleToM (ICLR 2026 version): explicit versus applied theory of mind
finding: Reasoning models still fail applied ToM. Nearly all models infer who knows what (mental state) at 95%+, but behaviour judgment is low. The gap shrinks but remains for o1, o3-mini, GPT-5 and DeepSeek-R1. This is the 2025-26 evidence for gap 2, on a related design (not Ullman or FANToM twins).
numbers: Mental state / behaviour prediction / behaviour judgment, 1147 items per category, 95% CI about +/-2.5: GPT-4o 95.6/49.5/15.3. Claude-3.5-Sonnet 97.9/67.0/24.9. o1-mini 87.8/44.8/27.0. o1 98.6/58.8/32.5. o1 high effort 98.7/60.2/33.3. o3-mini 85.4/66.8/41.3. GPT-5 98.5/64.4/40.0. DeepSeek-R1 97.3/73.8/65.8. o1-preview 95.6/84.1/59.5.
limits: SimpleToM is not a perturbation-twin design; it compares question levels on the same story. Different reasoning-effort settings and temperatures across models. Row alignment of the extracted table was checked against the text for o1-preview, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and GPT-4o.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 partly closed: the gap is not gone for reasoning models, and it varies a lot (judgment 32.5 for o1 vs 65.8 for DeepSeek-R1). Ullman-style and FANToM-style twins on current models were not found.

source: Gu et al. (2026) SimpleToM test-time interventions
finding: Reminders, system-prompt hints and CoT do not reliably close the gap. A mental-state reminder helps most but unevenly. CoT helped some models and not others.
numbers: Behaviour judgment none / reminder / system prompt / CoT: GPT-4o 15.3/42.2/14.9/39.2. Llama-3.1-405B 10.0/25.8/9.9/35.2. Claude-3.5-Sonnet 24.9/84.1/27.1/39.4. Behaviour prediction with reminder rises above 80% for the three models tested.
limits: Only three models given these interventions. The reminder tells the model which fact matters, which is a hint a real agent will not always have.
agent_relevance: Confirms and sharpens K09: the best fix was a task-specific reminder, not a general reasoning step. A 'name the simpler rival' step is a general step and should be expected to be weaker.

source: Hu and Frank (2024) Auxiliary task demands mask the capabilities of smaller language models (COLM 2024)
finding: Lowering task demands (forced choice by log probability instead of free production; probability instead of metalinguistic judgment) raises scores, most for small models. Four domains tested, so this is more than the two studies earlier checked. Chain of thought was named as untested.
numbers: Interaction of model size with evaluation method: analogical reasoning z=2.631 p=0.009; grammaticality z=1.995 p=0.0461; word prediction t=7.654 p=0.005; reflective reasoning not significant. Open models from 1B to 70B (Pythia, OLMo, Gemma, Llama-2, Mistral).
quote: performance on a task is a function of the model's underlying knowledge, combined with the model's ability to interpret and perform the task
limits: Open models with log-probability access only. No chain-of-thought test, so the interaction with CoT is open. Pythia behaves differently from the rest.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly closed: the demand effect holds across four domains, but CoT interaction was not measured. For API-only models the forced-choice route may need logprobs that are not offered.

source: Golchin and Surdeanu (2024) Time travel in LLMs: tracing data contamination (ICLR 2024)
finding: Guided completion works on chat-API models with plain text calls and no log probabilities. Cost is small: 10 instances per split, temperature 0, 500 token cap. Best variant uses GPT-4 as a few-shot match judge.
numbers: 28 settings (GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 x 14 partitions of 7 datasets). Success against two human experts: GPT-4 judge variant 14/14 on GPT-4 and 13/14 on GPT-3.5. ROUGE-L variant 13/14 on GPT-4 but 7/14 (chance) on GPT-3.5. BLEURT 11/14 and 9/14. Baseline 'ChatGPT-Cheat?' 0/14 strict on GPT-4. Found GPT-4 contaminated with AG News, WNLI, XSum.
quote: Our approach starts by identifying potential contamination at the instance level
limits: Only seven datasets, two models, snapshots from June 2023. Truth labels are human judgments of the same completions, not known training sets. Cannot say what kind of contamination. Newer models may refuse to repeat text.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 answered for guided completion: yes on API-only models, about 10 prompts plus a judge call per partition. Power on a hidden-label setting is untested. Needs a prefix of the test item, so works on items you can see.

source: Oren et al. (2023) Proving test set contamination in black box language models
finding: The order test needs a log probability for the whole benchmark text, in canonical and shuffled order. It gives a provable false-positive rate but is not usable on chat APIs that do not return prompt log probs. It cannot see single exposures.
numbers: Canary study, 1.4B model trained from scratch: detects at duplication 10 or more (e.g. MNLI p=1.96e-11 at 10 copies, TruthfulQA 3.43e-13) on 1000-item sets. Duplication 1 not reliably detected (BoolQ p=0.156, HellaSwag p=0.478 sharded). Detection threshold about 4 copies. Public audit of Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, Pythia-1.4B, GPT-2 XL on 8 benchmarks: little evidence except ARC for Mistral and MMLU. 65 files in under 24 hours at 7B with 50 shards x 250 permutations.
limits: Needs token log probs of arbitrary text. Fails for items seen once. Only models up to 7B audited in practice.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 answered for the order test: not for typical API-only chat models (no prompt logprobs), and power is low below 4 copies. Prefer guided completion or rephrase-gap tests for APIs.

source: Yang et al. (2023) Rethinking benchmark and contamination with rephrased samples
finding: Paraphrase and translation evade n-gram and embedding decontamination, and training on rephrased test items inflates scores a lot. So paraphrase is a strong way to hide contamination, which also makes a paraphrase gap a sensitive check for it.
numbers: Llama-2-13B trained on rephrased MMLU test reaches 85.9 accuracy while undetectable by n-gram overlap. Fine-tuned Llama-2 and CodeLlama reach performance on par with GPT-4 on MMLU, GSM8K and HumanEval. Llama-2 report: over 10% of MMLU test highly contaminated; GPT-4 report: 25% of HumanEval.
limits: Deliberate fine-tuning on rephrased items, which is a stronger exposure than ordinary leakage. Does not rank paraphrase against name, number or format swaps.
agent_relevance: Gap 4, partial: supports paraphrase as the first check because contamination hides under paraphrase, but no head-to-head per-token comparison exists in this folder.

source: Dekoninck, Muller and Vechev (2024) ConStat: performance-based contamination detection
finding: Defines contamination as inflated performance that does not carry to rephrased samples, synthetic samples or a related benchmark. Needs only scores, so it works on black-box models, but needs reference models. A leave-one-out check found sample-specific contamination in some reputable reference models.
numbers: Cost of building benchmarks about 300 USD on the OpenAI API plus 263 USD on the Together API and one month on one H100 for the whole study. Benjamini-Hochberg control at 5% false discovery. Sample-specific contamination: four instances in the reference models at p<0.5%. Phi models show GSM8k effect over 15% (p<0.01%), which the authors attribute to reasoning-focused training.
limits: Needs reference models of comparable skill. Effect can be confounded by training style (GSM8k vs MathQA). Cost figures are for the whole study, not per model.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 and 7, partial: the generalisation-gap view matches our default-minus-counterfactual idea. It shows the gap can come from training style, not only leakage, so a gap alone does not prove contamination.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying language models' sensitivity to spurious features in prompt design (ICLR 2024)
finding: Meaning-preserving format changes move accuracy a lot, so a single prompt format is not a trustworthy pass. FormatSpread explores formats within a budget and works on API models.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B across formats. GPT-3.5: spread up to 56 points, median 6.4, over 320 formats and 53 tasks, under 10 USD per task on average. Sensitivity persists with larger models, more shots and instruction tuning. Format performance correlates only weakly between models.
limits: Few-shot, classification-style tasks, not agent loops or free reasoning. Median spread (6.4) is far smaller than the maximum.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 and 5: format swap is expensive to ignore. A single pass has a typical error of several points and a worst case of tens of points. Report a range over formats, not one score.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2024) State of what art? A call for multi-prompt LLM evaluation
finding: Models rank differently across semantically equivalent instruction paraphrases. Single-template evaluation gives brittle rankings.
numbers: 6.5M instances, 20 LLMs, 39 tasks from 3 benchmarks. Kendall's W between templates is weak (about .27 to .54) on many LMentry tasks, medium (about .63 to .78) on several BIG-bench Hard tasks. A model can be best on one paraphrase and worst on another.
limits: Rankings across models, not absolute accuracy of one agent. Counts of paraphrases (11-16 per task) are modest.
agent_relevance: Gap 5, partial: no single rule for how many rephrasings, but the evidence is that 1 template is not enough and that around 10 paraphrases per task were used to expose ranking change. For one agent, report mean and worst over several paraphrases.

source: Gandhi et al. (2023) Understanding social reasoning in language models with language models (BigToM)
finding: Auto-generated causal-template ToM items with true-belief and false-belief pairs. GPT-4 reaches about human level on some inference types and others do not. On backward belief inference models are often far below chance. Weak models look fine when no false-belief condition is present.
numbers: Humans on backward belief inference: 82% true belief, 72% false belief. GPT-4 about human on forward action inference in the false-belief condition. Most other models far below chance on backward belief inference.
limits: Details per model were not tabulated here. Single research group. Humans rated a subset.
agent_relevance: Gap 6, partial: an independent group finds that only GPT-4 holds up in the false-belief condition, so claims for weaker models shrink under paired controls. No preregistered re-run by a different group of a published LLM ToM pass was found.

source: Search state: reasoning-model Ullman/FANToM twins and LLM replication gaps
finding: Searched for 2025-26 papers that re-run Ullman-style or FANToM-style twins on reasoning models, and for preregistered re-runs of published LLM ToM passes. WebSearch quota was used up and arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned 429, so the search could not be done. Direct PDF fetch of known ids worked.
numbers: 0 new twin-style studies found. This is an absence of search, not evidence of absence.
limits: Search coverage failed. Only papers I could name by id were opened.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 (twin form), 6 and 10 need a rerun of the search when quota returns. Do not read this as 'nobody has tested it'.

source: Absence check: tests of a rival-plus-probe or simplest-explanation operator against plain CoT
finding: The closest opened result is Huang 2024 (d05): a generic forced re-check hurts. Nothing opened tests a named-rival-plus-probe operator at equal tokens, nor a simplest-explanation rubric's false-negative rate.
numbers: 0 direct tests found; coverage limited as in d16.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1, 3 and 10 are experiments we must run. Use d05 as the warning: add a keep-answer path, count tokens, and measure right-to-wrong flips as well as gains.
